question: whats the email for reslife?? the heater in my room has been broken for like a week n nobody came

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Housing & Residence Life email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [1] Housing & Residence Life phone: (201) 684-7461; The Residence Life Mailroom: (201) 684-6639; Mackin Hall: (201) 684-7043; Bischoff Hall: (201) 684-7053; and five more on its page. [1] Housing & Residence Life is in The Lodge (CPA), which is on the campus map: [https://map.ramapo.edu/?id=2292#!m/1133346?sbc/](https://map.ramapo.edu/?id=2292#!m/1133346?sbc/). [3] Housing & Residence Life: Residents may contact the Resident Assistants at the Hall Office during posted hours of operation. The Residence Life Mailroom: orlmailroom@ramapo.edu Early Arrival: erlyariv@ramapo.edu Mackin Hall: mackin@ramapo.edu Bischoff Hall: bischoff@ramapo.edu Pine Hall: pine@ramapo.edu Overlook Hall: overlook@ramapo.edu College Park Apartments: cpa@ramapo.edu Laurel Hall: laurel@ramapo.edu The Village: village@ramapo.edu [1]

Housing & Residence Life's page "Heating Ventilating Air-Conditioning Units (HVAC)" says: "Please do not block HVAC units with furniture or personal belongings, and do not cover vents. Students who detect a smell or noise should submit a work order immediately. If smoke is visible, they should contact Public Safety immediately while vacating the area." (more on its page) [2] See Housing & Residence Life's page "The Office of Facilities and Work Orders". [2] See Housing & Residence Life's page "Facilities Emergencies and After Hours Emergencies". [2]

Facilities Management phone: (201) 684-7660; Receiving / Storeroom: (201) 684-7670. [4] Facilities Management is in P-FAC. [4] Facilities Management: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit [https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/](https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. [4]

Facilities Management's page "Building Maintenance – Repairs & Trades" says: "All emergencies are responded to as quickly as possible. Routine work requests are scheduled by the Supervisors. To request services click on the button below. Service Request Form ([https://ramapocollege.webtma.com/app/request/d4d71f56-79f4-47b2-98d6-5a7b536b4f2a](https://ramapocollege.webtma.com/app/request/d4d71f56-79f4-47b2-98d6-5a7b536b4f2a)) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660." (more on its page) [5] See Facilities Management's page "How to Submit a Facilities Work Request". [6] Facilities Management doesn't publish a general email address on its own pages (checked November 18, 2026). [4]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [3](https://map.ramapo.edu/?id=2292#!m/1133346?sbc/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-request-portal/)

body.answer:
The directory lists Paul Reck, Assistant Professor of Sociology; his courses include Criminology, Sociology of Deviance, Race Relations, Social Issues, and Introduction to Sociology. [4] It doesn’t identify who teaches LAWS 334 Juvenile Justice or LAWS 346 Victims and the Law. LAWS 334 is 4 credits, has no published prerequisites, and covers delinquency and the juvenile justice system. [2] LAWS 346 is 4 credits and has no published prerequisites; the catalog describes its focus as victims in the crime and criminal justice context. [3] For more information about a class before registering, contact the professor directly by email. [25] Contact the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office to ask who teaches these electives.

**School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7625; (201) 684-7562. Email: SSSWOffice@ramapo.edu. Office: ASB-431. [30]

What is a CRN and how do I find it?
A course registration number (CRN) is a unique five digit code assigned to a specific section of a course for registration.
You can find CRNs by:
Going to web.ramapo.edu and log into RCNJ Experience. You will log in with your Ramapo username (without the @ramapo.edu) and password.
Click on the Registration box and click Open Registration Dashboard
Select Register for Classes and chose a term (e.g., Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter)
Stay on the Find Classes tab. Enter the Subject and Course number (e.g., PSYC 101), then click Search
The CRN will be the five digit unique code listed next to each specific section
How do I register using Course Registration Numbers (CRNS)?
On the registration screen, switch from Find Classes tab to the enter CRN tab.
Type in the 5 digit CRN.
Click “Add to Summary”, review your schedule, and click “Submit” in the bottom right hand corner. Your status will change from “Pending” to “Registered”.
What should I do if a class I need is full or closed?
Select a backup or alternate course: Check your DegreeWorks audit (https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/wp-content/uploads/sites/133/2025/06/How-to-Run-a-DegreeWorks-Audit.pdf) for your remaining requirements. Identify open sections offered at alternate times or check if a equivalent general education or major requirement can be taken instead.
Monitor during Add/Drop: Course offerings shift frequently during the first week of classes. Keep checking the Registration Dashboard for open seats.
How do I register for Career Pathways?
Going to web.ramapo.edu and log into RCNJ Experience. You will log in with your Ramapo username (without the @ramapo.edu) and password.
Click on the Registration box and click Open Registration Dashboard
Select Register for Classes and chose a term (e.g., Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter)
In the subject type in “Pathways” and for the course number type in which Career Pathways you are looking to take (e.g., 001, 002, 003)
Select the Pathways correlated with your Academic School (you will see this in the section column)

School of Science, Nursing and Health – SN1 or SN2
School of Social Sciences and Social Work – SO1 or SO2
Susan and Nick Vallario School of Arts, Humanities, and Education – AH1 or AH2
*Career Pathways is a half-semester course. For example, sections with AH1 are in the first half of the semester while sections marked AH2 would be in the second half*

question: when is the math dept office open? need someone to sign an override for linear algebra bc the section is full

body.answer:
I don’t have verified information about the math department office’s hours. For an override, the Registrar says to see the course instructor to obtain an electronic override, provide the instructor with specific information about the kind of override needed, and then register online after the override is entered [6]. The Registrar also says that sometimes you may obtain special permission from the instructor for a closed course; after receiving an electronic override, you must register for the course [7]. For instructor-signature permission, obtain permission from the instructor; if granted, the instructor places an override on your record, and you must complete registration in Web Self-Service: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/?name=homepage&accessibility=true](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/?name=homepage&accessibility=true) [8]. The Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) says to contact the course instructor or school office to request permission to override [9]. Contact the Science, Nursing and Health school office about its hours.

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [24]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [24]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/registration-faq/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

I don’t have verified information about the math department office’s hours. For an override, the Registrar says to see the course instructor to obtain an electronic override, provide the instructor with specific information about the kind of override needed, and then register online after the override is entered [6]. The Registrar also says that sometimes you may obtain special permission from the instructor for a closed course; after receiving an electronic override, you must register for the course [7]. For instructor-signature permission, obtain permission from the instructor; if granted, the instructor places an override on your record, and you must complete registration in Web Self-Service: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/?name=homepage&accessibility=true](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/?name=homepage&accessibility=true) [8]. The Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) says to contact the course instructor or school office to request permission to override [9]. Contact the Science, Nursing and Health school office about its hours.

question: who runs the writing center? i wanna apply to be a tutor there

body.answer:
The Center for Reading and Writing’s Outreach Coordinator is Priscilla Tovey [9].

To apply to be a peer consultant, the Center for Reading and Writing requires successful completion of CRWT 102 (or AIID 201, if you placed out of CRWT); a minimum GPA of 3.3 (or strong evidence of exemplary academic improvement after a GPA-crushing crisis); evidence you can work independently and in a close-knit group; evidence of motivation to help others; availability for all-day pre-service training during the week before fall semester begins; and availability to work at least ten hours per week and attend in-service training during the academic year [4].

There is no application form. Submit together a one-page cover letter addressing your claims to the requirements, an unofficial copy of your current academic transcript, and a resume [4]. Submit electronically to Handshake, Ramapo’s student employment website, at the Writing & Reading Peer Consultants link: [https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/handshake-students/](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/handshake-students/) [4]. The job is posted in March and remains on Handshake until all positions are filled [4]. Questions? Contact Priscilla Tovey at ptovey@ramapo.edu [4].

- **Center for Reading and Writing**: Phone: (201) 684-7557. Email: crw@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons, Room 420. Outreach Coordinator: LC-424; Developmental Writing Specialist: LC-425; Reading Specialist: LC-423. [16]
- **Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [16]

The Center for Reading and Writing’s Outreach Coordinator is Priscilla Tovey [9].

To apply to be a peer consultant, the Center for Reading and Writing requires successful completion of CRWT 102 (or AIID 201, if you placed out of CRWT); a minimum GPA of 3.3 (or strong evidence of exemplary academic improvement after a GPA-crushing crisis); evidence you can work independently and in a close-knit group; evidence of motivation to help others; availability for all-day pre-service training during the week before fall semester begins; and availability to work at least ten hours per week and attend in-service training during the academic year [4].

There is no application form. Submit together a one-page cover letter addressing your claims to the requirements, an unofficial copy of your current academic transcript, and a resume [4]. How do I apply for Clinical Practice?
Teacher candidates must first schedule an appointment with Ms. Joanne Caselli, Teacher Education Certification Officer, to ensure all requirements for Clinical Practice have been met.
Once Ms. Caselli provides clearance, teacher candidates may submit their top three school districts of choice through the Teacher Education Department (TED) online portal.
For questions related to applying for Clinical Practice, please contact:
How am I evaluated throughout Clinical Practice?
There are two types of assessment instruments used to evaluate performance throughout Clinical Practice.
The Observation and Conference Report (OCR) is a performance-based, formative assessment instrument used to provide feedback to clinical interns on observed lessons. The OCR is used by both clinical supervisors and cooperating teachers during Clinical Practice I and Clinical Practice II. The OCR contains eleven (11) indicators that align to the New Jersey Professional Standards for Teachers (NJPST) and Interstate Teacher Assessment Consortium (InTASC) standards.
During Clinical Practice I, clinical supervisors observe their assigned clinical interns teach three (3) separate lessons and hold a conference to deliver feedback after each observed lesson. Clinical supervisors must complete and submit a digital Observation and Conference Report after each formal observation/post-observation conference. Interns’ cooperating teachers must do the same, but only once during Clinical Practice I. It is encouraged that cooperating teachers’ observations/post-observation conferences coincide with one of the supervisors’ observations and post-observation conferences, if possible.
During Clinical Practice II, clinical supervisors observe their assigned clinical interns teach six (6) separate lessons and hold a conference to deliver feedback after each observed lesson. Clinical supervisors must complete and submit a digital Observation and Conference Report after each observation/post-observation conference. Interns’ cooperating teachers must do the same, but only one during Clinical Practice II. It is encouraged that cooperating teachers’ observations/post-observation conferences coincide with two of the supervisors’ observations and post-observation conferences, if possible.
Please see Appendix J for the Observation and Conference Report.
The Clinical Competency Inventory (CCI) is a performance-based observational instrument designed to provide actionable feedback on the progress of individual clinical interns completing Clinical Practice. The CCI is a standards-based assessment rubric that measures key competencies aligned to the 2013 InTASC standards, 2014 New Jersey Professional Standards for Teachers, and the current Educative Teacher Performance Assessment (edTPA) rubrics. A haunting and original exhibition about the Holocaust by Prague artists Gabriela Bulisova and Mark Isaac.
Co-sponsored and co-produced by the Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies at Ramapo College, with additional sponsorship by the Sara & Sam Schoffer Holocaust Resource Center at Stockton University and the Stockton University Art Gallery.
The Landscape of our Memory is a long-term artistic project that addresses the “dispersed Holocaust” or “Holocaust by Bullets” by commemorating the more than 2 million individuals who were killed in or near their hometowns rather than in major extermination camps. Inspired by the work of academics studying the Environmental History of the Holocaust (a relatively new sub-field of Holocaust studies), the artists use multiple antique and contemporary strategies to, in the words of the late Austrian historian Martin Pollack, “restore the names, faces and stories” of those tragically lost. Initial work was created under the auspices of two Fulbright Scholar grants in Poland, but the project now includes commemorations of those who lost their lives at the Terezin transit camp in the Czech Republic and will soon expand to other locations, including sites in Ukraine and Slovakia. Because every artistic technique is deeply rooted in the landscape, the project has an important environmental sensibility and begins a conversation about the relationship between genocide and ecocide. Ramapo Curatorial Prize exhibition, curated by Zuhra Amini featuring artists who work with fraught histories.
Fraction/Refraction brings together Kerr Cirilo, Clare Hu, and Basharat Ali Syed, whose image-based works push and pull highlighted, forgotten, or obscured layers of history to offer entry points into its constructed truths. The title references the scientific process of refraction whereby a wave bends as it passes through at least two mediums of differing densities, altering the wave’s speed and direction. The exhibition considers how national narratives bend in relation to the density of images that alter personal and collective memories. Cirilo, Hu, and Syed each focus on their encounters with parts and pieces of saturated, neglected, and exploited images sourced from archives, documentaries, and online databases within their areas of research. In a time when images are easily distrusted, the artists in this exhibition are concerned with the vulnerability of images. Fraction, Refraction makes a case for looking beyond the image at face value to tune into the labor and process by which political narratives are shaped in its failure.
The Ramapo Curatorial Prize is awarded each year to a second-year graduate student at Bard College’s Center for Curatorial Studies.

body.answer:
I don’t have verified information about a December tree lighting. The Traditions Council is charged with preserving Ramapo College traditions and fostering new traditions; traditions are activities passed down year to year with academic, celebratory, symbolic or historic meaning, unique to the Ramapo experience. LINCOLN, Nebraska (April 4, 2024) – Ramapo College was honored with 2023 Tree Campus Higher Education recognition by the Arbor Day Foundation for its commitment to effective urban forest management.
The Arbor Day Foundation is the world’s largest membership nonprofit organization dedicated to planting trees. Its Tree Campus Higher Education program began in 2008 to encourage colleges and universities to plant trees on their campuses.
Trees on campus and in urban spaces can lower energy costs by providing shade cover, cleaner air and water, and green spaces for students and faculty. In addition, trees improve students’ mental and cognitive health, provide an appealing aesthetic for campuses, and create shaded areas for studying and gathering.
“Trees not only play a vital role in the environment but also in our daily lives,” said Dan Lambe, chief executive of the Arbor Day Foundation. “Having trees on college and university campuses is a great way to show a commitment to students and faculty’s overall wellbeing.”
The Tree Campus Higher Education program honors colleges and universities for effective campus forest management and engaging staff and students in conservation goals. Ramapo College achieved the distinction by meeting Tree Campus Higher Education’s five standards, including maintaining a tree advisory committee, a campus tree-care plan, dedicated annual expenditures for its campus tree program, an Arbor Day observance, and student service-learning project. Currently, there are 411 campuses across the United States with this recognition. Ramapo College is the only college or university to earn this recognition in the State of New Jersey, and this is the fourth year in a row that Ramapo College has earned this recognition.
“It’s not by accident that we have a beautiful campus as we take our responsibility to be good stewards of this land seriously so that future generations can live healthy lives here,” said Dr. Michael Yankovich, Vice President for Operational and Administrative Integration at Ramapo College. “I’m particularly proud of our tree advisory committee, which includes students, faculty, facilities management, and community members. While responsibility for campus trees ultimately lies with the facilities department, the Campus Tree Advisory Committee provides guidance for future planning, helps develop the comprehensive campus tree plan, and educates the community about the benefits of the campus trees. We have a great team that works collaboratively, and I’d particularly like to highlight the commitment and professionalism of Ed Roessler, our campus grounds manager, and Dr. Eric Weiner, associate professor of environmental science.”

Individuals with hearing impairments may use a variety of communication methods, including lipreading, amplification, American Sign Language (ASL) and others. Some students may use interpreters in class. While the presence of an interpreter may initially feel distracting, classes typically adapt to the interpreter’s presence fairly quickly. Some students who have residual hearing may use a personal FM transmitter/receiver unit (a simple device worn by the instructor).
Examples of ways impairment may affect a student’s ability to participate include:
Difficulty following lectures in large halls, particularly if the acoustics cause echoes or if the speaker talks quietly, quickly, or unclearly.
Difficulty simultaneously watching demonstrations and following verbal instructions or descriptions, particularly if the student is watching a sign language interpreter, a captioning screen, or the speaker’s lips.
Difficulty following and participating in classroom discussions, particularly if the discussions is fast-paced and unmoderated, as there is often a lag time between a speaker’s comments and interpretation.
Students with hearing impairments may communicate via:
Lipreading
Amplification
American Sign Language (ASL)
Students who are deaf may have little or no speech depending on the severity of the hearing loss and the age of onset. They will often communicate through a certified sign language interpreter. The presence of an interpreter may initially feel distracting; however, both professors and students typically adapt to the interpreter’s presence fairly quickly.
Potential Accommodations / Teaching Strategies:
Seating close to the instructor
Captioned videos and movies
Use of an Interpreter
Note: When an interpreter is used, speak to the student, not to the interpreter. Speak naturally without exaggerating lip movement or volume. Be sure that the interpreter is clearly visible. (Be careful of darker rooms or window glare.)
During class discussions, ensure that no more than one person speaks at a time
Repeat questions and comments made by other students
Include visual media in presenting course information
Avoid giving information while handing out papers or writing on the board
When reading directly from a text, provide an advance copy; pause briefly when interjecting information not in the text
When working with the chalkboard or an overhead projection, pause briefly so that the student may look first at the board and then at the interpreter, to see what is being said
Oral tests with an interpreter
Extended testing time
For courses that include field trips or internships, OSS can help identify and coordinate accommodations.

question: do greek orgs have a gpa requirement? also im a d3 athlete is it even realistic to join one w practice every day

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): It can be realistic, but daily practice may make it tough to balance classes, sleep, and other commitments. Ask about the organization’s expected hours, required attendance, and flexibility during busy weeks before joining, and be honest about what you can consistently manage.

Yes. To participate in recruitment, accept a bid, and join, you must have earned 12–23 Ramapo credits and have a cumulative 2.5 GPA or better, or have earned 24 Ramapo credits or more and have a cumulative 2.25 GPA or better. You must also be in good academic standing, not on disciplinary probation, and be a full-time enrolled student. Transfer students may join in their first semester without meeting eligibility requirements other than being in good standing. You must attend one in-person Hazing Prevention Workshop, sign the New Member Process Acknowledgment, and complete the required online courses assigned by the Coordinator of Fraternities, Sororities, and Student Organizations. [2]

The time commitment varies by chapter; the first semester is time intensive because of the new member education program. As a general member, expect weekly chapter meetings, community service, and study hours. Events are generally planned in advance so students can coordinate schedules. [3] The information doesn’t say whether a daily practice schedule is manageable for an athlete. Ask the Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life and the chapter you’re considering about its new-member schedule. [3][6]

**Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life**: Email: ofsl@ramapo.edu. [24]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/greek/recruitment/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/greek/frequently-asked-questions-faq/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/greek/recruitment/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

The Chair, when present, shall preside at all meetings of the Board and Executive/Judicial Committee. The Treasurer shall serve as a member of the Resources Committee and the Audit Committee. The Treasurer shall oversee through their Committee service, the Board’s review of and action related to the Board’s financial responsibilities.

The Board shall meet at its principal office or at such other place as the Chair of the Board shall from time to time designate.

question: our club put in a budget request for spring last week, has it been approved yet??

body.answer:
I can’t verify whether your request has been approved. If it was a SPIF request, the general process is that applications are due in late February, SRAB evaluates submissions in March, recommendations go to IEC, and final decisions are made by the President’s Senior Leadership Team after the College’s Budget is approved by the Board of Trustees. OIEP informs applicants shortly thereafter. [1] Contact Student Government Association to ask about your club’s request. The new Request To Fill process (https://www.ramapo.edu/poerd/request-to-fill-procedures/) (RTF), will provide added oversight so that all people resources will be allocated and aligned with overall strategic goals and critical operational need. question: whats genetics like at ramapo is it mostly lecture or is there a lab part too? sophomore bio tryna plan spring

body.answer:
Genetics has both a lecture and a lab: BIOL 332 is 4 credits, and BIOL 332L is 1.5 credits. The catalog describes the subject as inheritance and gene action, covering Mendelian principles, transmission and molecular genetics, genetic mapping, population and quantitative genetics, and genomics in lecture and laboratory. [2][3]

To take BIOL 332, you need one of BIOL 112; BIOL 113 and BIOL 113L; BIOL 215; or BIOL 216 and BIOL 216L; one of CHEM 110 or CHEM 116 and CHEM 116L; and CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S. You must also be enrolled in BIOL 332L. [2] For BIOL 332L, those same listed prerequisite alternatives apply, and you must be enrolled in BIOL 332; the lab has a course fee and a WRITING INTENSIVE (WRIT) attribute. [3] The catalog lists each as a corequisite of the other, so they may be taken together. [2][3]

To check whether they’re offered in spring, go to the Dynamic Class Schedule, select the correct term, click SUBMIT, then filter as needed by subject, course number, title, credit range, course level, attribute type, start and end time, or day of week. [11]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL332) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL332L) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/summer/undergraduate/)

answer:
Genetics has both a lecture and a lab: BIOL 332 is 4 credits, and BIOL 332L is 1.5 credits. The catalog describes the subject as inheritance and gene action, covering Mendelian principles, transmission and molecular genetics, genetic mapping, population and quantitative genetics, and genomics in lecture and laboratory. [2][3]

To take BIOL 332, you need one of BIOL 112; BIOL 113 and BIOL 113L; BIOL 215; or BIOL 216 and BIOL 216L; one of CHEM 110 or CHEM 116 and CHEM 116L; and CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S. You must also be enrolled in BIOL 332L. [2] For BIOL 332L, those same listed prerequisite alternatives apply, and you must be enrolled in BIOL 332; the lab has a course fee and a WRITING INTENSIVE (WRIT) attribute. [3] The catalog lists each as a corequisite of the other, so they may be taken together. [2][3]

To check whether they’re offered in spring, go to the Dynamic Class Schedule, select the correct term, click SUBMIT, then filter as needed by subject, course number, title, credit range, course level, attribute type, start and end time, or day of week. [11]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL332) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL332L) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/summer/undergraduate/)

body.answer:
First-Year Seminar (INTD 101) is 4 credits and has no published prerequisites. [1] It’s a general-education course designed to help first-year students adjust to college-level learning. You choose a seminar topic that interests you; classes use discussion, critical reading, writing, and research or problem-solving assignments, and may include experiential learning. [1][3][4] All incoming first-year students read a common summer book and discuss it in the seminar. [4]

Yes. First-Year Seminar is a general education requirement for first-year students, taken during the fall semester of their first year. [2]

**First-Year Seminar**: Phone: Director of First-Year Seminar (201) 684-6254. [14]

First-Year Seminar (INTD 101) is 4 credits and has no published prerequisites. [1] It’s a general-education course designed to help first-year students adjust to college-level learning. You choose a seminar topic that interests you; classes use discussion, critical reading, writing, and research or problem-solving assignments, and may include experiential learning. FINC 301 prerequisites are ACCT 221, BADM 225, CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S, and one of MATH 101, MATH 108, MATH 110, or MATH 121. Neither ECON 101 nor ECON 102 is listed as a FINC 301 prerequisite. [2]
If you’re asking about the Finance BS, both ECON 101 (Microeconomics) and ECON 102 (Introduction to Macroeconomics) are required courses in the degree; that is separate from FINC 301’s prerequisites. [1]

question: can i take microbio next semester if i finished bio 1 but im only in bio 2 rn

body.answer:
For BIOL 311 Microbiology Lecture and BIOL 311L Microbiology Laboratory, the listed biology options are BIOL 110, BIOL 111 with BIOL 111L, BIOL 112, or BIOL 113 with BIOL 113L. You must also meet one listed chemistry option; any chemistry prerequisite option may be completed concurrently with the course. BIOL 311 and BIOL 311L are corequisites, so you must enroll in both. [1][2] If you mean the BIOL 212 Microbiology for Health Science lecture and lab, its prerequisite is one of BIOL 213, BIOL 214 with BIOL 214L, CHEM 111 with CHEM 111L, or CHEM 115; the lecture and lab are corequisites. [3][4] The catalog lists BIOL 111 as Fundamentals of Biology I and BIOL 113 as Fundamentals of Biology II; BIOL 113 requires BIOL 111 with BIOL 111L (or BIOL 110), and enrollment in BIOL 113L. [5][6] So finishing Bio 1 alone does not establish that you meet all microbiology prerequisites; your Bio 1/Bio 2 course numbers and lab completion matter. I don't have verified information about which courses you personally finished or are taking. Contact the School of Science, Nursing, and Health Office to confirm your eligibility. [7]

**School of Science, Nursing, and Health Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7734. Email: SNHOffice@ramapo.edu. Office: ASB-422. [19]

body.answer:
The Sustainability Minor requires ENST 209 WORLD SUSTAINABILITY and SUST 410 SENIOR PRECAPSTONE, plus 3 elective courses from its listed options; at least one elective must be at the 300-level. That is 5 courses total, and the catalog does not give a total credit count for the minor. [1]

The catalog does not say which courses you personally can double-count. College policy allows some courses fulfilling a primary or secondary major to count toward a minor, but they may not exceed one-half of the credits required in the minor. [13] Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) to confirm what applies to your Biology major.

question: Im double majoring in psychology and criminology. Can one course count toward both majors or do I need completely separate classes for each?

body.answer:
Yes. For students with two majors, no more than half the courses can double-count in both majors. All writing-intensive courses required for the second major must be completed as well. [9]

For your Psychology BA and Sociology BA with a Criminology concentration, check with the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office about applying that rule to your specific courses. [1][2]

**School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7625; (201) 684-7562. Email: SSSWOffice@ramapo.edu. Office: ASB-431. [17]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-SOCI) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can seniors take a grad class n have it count for undergrad credit? thinking abt the mba later

body.answer:
The Office of the Provost says a matriculated undergraduate in good standing needs positive endorsement from their academic advisor and permission from the graduate program’s Director. You may take up to TWO graduate courses (no more than 8 credits) during your undergraduate career, and must be on track to complete at least 32 credits at Ramapo. The course is billed at undergraduate tuition and fees. [2]

For undergraduates pursuing a 4+1 program, the policy allows ONE ADDITIONAL graduate course, up to THREE TOTAL (no more than 12 credits) billed at the undergraduate tuition rate. You may register for up to 8 graduate credits in a semester and may not take more than 50% of your semester credit load in graduate-level courses. Undergraduate students cannot take 600-level or higher MBAD (MBA) courses. The course counts toward undergraduate degree requirements and, if you later matriculate in a Ramapo graduate program, may also be used toward its requirements if applicable. [3]

The MBA page says non-business undergraduates can take up to two 500-level MBA courses while completing undergraduate studies; students granted Advanced Standing are not eligible to take MBA courses as undergraduates. [7] The MBA FAQ says to apply during the first semester of senior year. [10] Contact the Office of the Provost and the MBA program Director about eligibility and permission.

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [17]

answer:
The Office of the Provost says a matriculated undergraduate in good standing needs positive endorsement from their academic advisor and permission from the graduate program’s Director. You may take up to TWO graduate courses (no more than 8 credits) during your undergraduate career, and must be on track to complete at least 32 credits at Ramapo. The course is billed at undergraduate tuition and fees. [2]

For undergraduates pursuing a 4+1 program, the policy allows ONE ADDITIONAL graduate course, up to THREE TOTAL (no more than 12 credits) billed at the undergraduate tuition rate. You may register for up to 8 graduate credits in a semester and may not take more than 50% of your semester credit load in graduate-level courses. Undergraduate students cannot take 600-level or higher MBAD (MBA) courses. The course counts toward undergraduate degree requirements and, if you later matriculate in a Ramapo graduate program, may also be used toward its requirements if applicable. [3]

The MBA page says non-business undergraduates can take up to two 500-level MBA courses while completing undergraduate studies; students granted Advanced Standing are not eligible to take MBA courses as undergraduates. [7] The MBA FAQ says to apply during the first semester of senior year. [10] Contact the Office of the Provost and the MBA program Director about eligibility and permission.

question: I'm 41 and thinking about coming back to school. Does Ramapo offer any certificate programs I could do part time or in the evenings, instead of a full degree?

body.answer:
Yes. The catalog lists these certificates: Applied Ethics Certificate; Business Essentials Certificate; Business Foundations-Graduate Certificate; Data Analyst-Graduate Certificate; Data Modeler-Graduate Certificate; Machine Learning Engineer-Graduate Certificate; Spanish for Health Care and Human Services Professionals Certificate. [5]

For Business Essentials, the certificate may be completed during one or two summers, and students are guaranteed seats during Summer Sessions. Course sections are offered at convenient times, including online or in the evening; some are also offered online during the four-week Winter Session. [26]

The adult Degree Completion Program serves students 25 and older and offers part-time and evening options, but it leads to a bachelor’s degree, not a certificate. [6][8]

**Degree Completion Program**: Phone: Director, Degree Completion Program (201) 684-7388. Email: complete@ramapo.edu. [28]

Sources: [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/faqs/) [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/asb/essentials/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do u set up an independent study w a professor? is there a form and can it count for my major

body.answer:
The Registrar says limited opportunities are available. Find an instructor, have the Independent Study Registration Form completed by the instructor and the dean of the sponsoring school, then return it to the Registrar’s Office. Graduate studies also require the graduate program director. [3] Students must also complete a contract form covering the purpose, objective, grading criteria, hours of work, discipline and level, and title/credits. [3] The registration form is linked here: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Independent-Study-Registration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Independent-Study-Registration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf). [4]

Undergraduates may take no more than FOUR (4) credits per semester, including summer or winter, and normally may not exceed eight credits over their career. Students on academic probation or warning need the Dean’s permission; you cannot take an Independent Study for a course offered in that semester’s regular schedule. Registration is not accepted after the last day of add/drop in the academic calendar. [3]

Whether it can count for your major depends on the program; no program requirements in the catalog list INTD 300 or INTD 400. [1] INTD 300 and INTD 400 are each 4 credits, with no published prerequisites. [1][2] Contact the Registrar about the form and registration, and your school dean about whether a study can count toward your major.

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/INTD300) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/INTD400) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/forms-transcripts/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

The Registrar says limited opportunities are available. Find an instructor, have the Independent Study Registration Form completed by the instructor and the dean of the sponsoring school, then return it to the Registrar’s Office. Graduate studies also require the graduate program director. [3] Students must also complete a contract form covering the purpose, objective, grading criteria, hours of work, discipline and level, and title/credits. [3] The registration form is linked here: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Independent-Study-Registration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Independent-Study-Registration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf). [4]

Undergraduates may take no more than FOUR (4) credits per semester, including summer or winter, and normally may not exceed eight credits over their career. Students on academic probation or warning need the Dean’s permission; you cannot take an Independent Study for a course offered in that semester’s regular schedule. Registration is not accepted after the last day of add/drop in the academic calendar. [3]

Whether it can count for your major depends on the program; no program requirements in the catalog list INTD 300 or INTD 400. question: worked in IT for like 12 yrs before coming back. can i get credit by exam or CLEP out of the intro classes? and how many credits do i actually have to take AT ramapo to get the degree

body.answer:
Your IT experience may qualify for Prior Learning Assessment (PLA): a portfolio can demonstrate knowledge matching a Ramapo course. Undergraduate PLA portfolios are limited to 16 credits; they cannot duplicate credit or cover your final 32 degree credits, and apply to 100–300-level courses only (not capstones). To pursue it, meet with the Degree Completion Program Director, then the appropriate Dean; if approved, work with an assigned faculty assessor to prepare a portfolio and signed PLA Portfolio Contract. The fee must be paid before review. [7][11] Contact the Degree Completion Program about PLA. [14]

CLEP can award credit for INFO 224: Information Systems and Computer Applications, score 50, 4 credits. [22] Ramapo students must request the online Off-Campus Study Form from the Center for Student Success before registering. [24] Send official CLEP scores from College Board; after evaluation, Ramapo emails a Transfer Credit Evaluation showing accepted courses and credits. [26]

For the Information Technology Management BS, the catalog plan requires 128 credits total. [1] At least 48 credits must be completed at Ramapo, with the final 32 in residence. [15] Contact Admissions to have CLEP scores or prior coursework evaluated. [26]

- **Degree Completion Program**: Phone: Director, Degree Completion Program (201) 684-7388. Email: complete@ramapo.edu. [27]
- **Testing Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: testing@ramapo.edu. Location: Laurel Hall, North. [27]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-INFM) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/pla/) [11](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-for-prior-learning) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/clep-subjects/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/clep/) [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/freshmen/faqs/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

GPLA credit may be granted for equivalent coursework offered at Ramapo College.

GPLA credits are awarded a TP or "transfer pass" grade, so they are not calculated in the student’s GPA.

Criteria for graduate prior learning assessment (GPLA)
Criteria for acceptance of prior learning experiences include:
The experience must be relevant to the program’s learning goals.
The experience must be comparable to graduate-level coursework.
The experience must have taken place after the awarding of the bachelor’s degree and before enrollment in the graduate program.
The student must document and submit a GPLA portfolio by the deadline agreed upon by the student and the Program Director but no later than the end of the first semester enrolled in the graduate program.

GPLA requirements
When a graduate student applies to Ramapo College, they are made aware of the opportunity to apply for GPLA. (Note: GPLA information is provided on the Graduate Admissions website.) GPLA requirements include:
Prior learning experience may be substituted for up to two (2) courses (not to exceed 8 credits) in the graduate program.

The Program Director or designee reviews and evaluates applications for prior learning credit and recommends the number of credits to be awarded. The Dean makes the final approval.
GPLA credit may be granted for equivalent coursework offered at Ramapo College.
When the experience does not compare to a Ramapo course but falls within the purview of the evaluator’s expertise, credit may be granted as an elective.
GPLA credits are awarded a TP or "transfer pass" grade, so they are not calculated in the student’s GPA.
All GPLA documentation, including the portfolio and assessment rubric, are kept in the student’s permanent record. Credits earned through GPLA are reflected in the graduate degree audit.
Criteria for graduate prior learning assessment (GPLA)
Criteria for acceptance of prior learning experiences include:
The experience must be relevant to the program’s learning goals.
The experience must be comparable to graduate-level coursework.
The experience must have taken place after the awarding of the bachelor’s degree and before enrollment in the graduate program.
The student must document and submit a GPLA portfolio by the deadline agreed upon by the student and the Program Director but no later than the end of the first semester enrolled in the graduate program.

question: im undeclared, by when do i have to declare a major? like is there a credit limit or smth

body.answer:
You must declare a major by the time you have earned 64 credits toward the graduation requirement. If you have at least 48 credits and register for additional credits, the Center for Student Success will notify you that you must declare before registering for more than 64 credits. If you try to register for 64 or more credits without declaring, a registration hold will prevent registration. Submit the online Major/Minor Declaration form to the Office of the Registrar; after receiving it, the Registrar removes the hold and you can register. [1]

For a four-year graduation goal, the Center for Student Success recommends aiming to declare sometime during sophomore year; most majors take at least two years to complete. [5]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [32]
- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [32]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#declaring-a-major1) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
You must declare a major by the time you have earned 64 credits toward the graduation requirement. If you have at least 48 credits and register for additional credits, the Center for Student Success will notify you that you must declare before registering for more than 64 credits. If you try to register for 64 or more credits without declaring, a registration hold will prevent registration. Submit the online Major/Minor Declaration form to the Office of the Registrar; after receiving it, the Registrar removes the hold and you can register. [1]

For a four-year graduation goal, the Center for Student Success recommends aiming to declare sometime during sophomore year; most majors take at least two years to complete. [5]

question: whats my registration time for spring? i cant find it

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that! I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I can’t tell your exact time without your earned-credit total. For Spring 2027, times are based on credits earned as of September 30, 2026; currently enrolled credits don’t count. Check earned credits on your transcript or degree audit (excluding non-degree courses, unresolved Incompletes, W’s and F’s), then compare them with the schedule at [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/). [6]

To see your assigned window: go to Experience, locate the Registration Card, click Open Registration Dashboard, then click Register for Classes. [6] You should also have received an email from the Registrar’s Office the week of October 20 with your window. [6] Undergraduate registration windows are assigned by earned credits; your Academic Transcript shows your earned credits. [1]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/registration-faq/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: do ramapo students get any discount on nj transit? i take the bus n train a lot

body.answer:
Yes. Students can save 25% on already discounted NJ Transit monthly passes: [https://www.njtransit.com/studentpass](https://www.njtransit.com/studentpass). Ramapo also says students can get one free month. [1][3]

For the student pass, go to Ramapo Self-Service, log in, click Web Self-Service, click Student Services and Financial Aid, click Online NJ Transit Student Pass, enroll, and follow the instructions. [13]

For bus travel, Ramapo's Coach USA/Shortline student one-way tickets are $9 with a valid Ramapo ID; tickets bought on the bus are full price ($13+). [2]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [35]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/about/transportation-services/public-transportation/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/about/transportation-services/public-transportation/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/about/transportation-services/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/get-started/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): It depends on the school, instructor, and your strengths, so there isn’t one science course that’s easiest for everyone. Introductory astronomy, geology, or environmental science can feel more approachable if you prefer less math, but check course syllabi and grade distributions where available before choosing.

I don’t have verified information about which science Gen Ed is easiest or most likely to earn an A. The catalog lists ENSC 103 INTRODUCTION TO ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE, GEOL 106 FUNDAMENTALS OF EARTH SCIENCE LECTURE, and GEOL 106L FUNDAMENTALS OF EARTH SCIENCE LAB as Scientific Reasoning Gen Eds. [30]

The chemistry major at Ramapo, offered by the School of Science, Nursing, and Health, gives its students an in-depth grasp of theoretical concepts as well as a variety of practical skills.
In the first year, students enroll in General Chemistry which provides an introduction to modern chemical theory presented through the study of atomic and molecular structure.
In the next three years, core courses in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, quantitative/instrumental analysis, physical chemistry and biochemistry contribute to a broad understanding of the structure and dynamics of atoms and molecules and their role in physical and chemical processes.
A selection of chemistry electives, including Cooperative Education placements, independent research study, and a broad range of special topic electives, allow senior students to concentrate in specialty areas such as materials development and characterization, synthetic organic chemistry, organometallic chemistry, biochemistry, and analytical/ environmental chemistry.
Many courses are offered by other science major programs allowing students to plan a multidisciplinary program of study.
Many of the scientific advances of this modern age occur in interdisciplinary areas such as biophysics, materials science, molecular biology, medicinal chemistry, protein biotechnology, and environmental science, consequently mixing courses from different scientific fields is certainly advantageous and desirable.
BIOCHEMISTRY:
Biochemistry is an interdisciplinary field concerned with the chemical composition, structure, and molecular functions of living organisms.
Knowledge derived from the disciplines of chemistry, physics, and biology is used to understand the processes that operate in cells and organisms, including their metabolism and regulation.
Biochemistry attempts to understand the uniqueness of complex evolving living systems:
How living organisms harvest energy from their environment to produce and maintain their complexity
How these structures replicate themselves.
The knowledge obtained from biochemical research has been applied to solve problems in areas ranging from agriculture to medicine.
Specific areas of biochemistry include principles of protein structure (amino acid chemistry, peptide and protein structure and protein folding), enzymes (mechanisms, enzyme kinetics and inhibition), nucleic acids (nucleotides and nucleic acid chemistry, DNA sequencing, protein and genetic engineering) and metabolism (carbohydrate structure, glucose catabolism, citric acid cycle).", "page_updated": "2022-01-31"}, {"n": 10, "heading": "Survival Tip #1", "page": "https://www.ramapo.edu/snh/biology/student-resources/", "text": "Go to class. General education requirements will be set by the faculty and approved by the Provost or designee.
Required courses include First-Year Seminar, Critical Reading and Writing II, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities. Assessment of general education is the responsibility of the faculty and, with the support of the Vice Provost, will be undertaken in a systematic and regularly occurring manner.
GECCo (General Education Curriculum Committee) oversees the assessment of the student learning outcomes for general education and recommends approval of general education courses to the Academic Review Committee, which, in turn, recommends final approval to the Provost.

question: how do u get a job on campus? do i need work study or can anyone apply. i work at a restaurant rn but would rather work somewhere between classes

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Start by deciding how many hours you can work around classes, then look for flexible part-time, seasonal, or remote roles. Prepare a simple résumé highlighting coursework, projects, volunteering, and transferable skills, and apply through job boards, nearby businesses, or your school’s career resources. Tailor each application, follow up politely, and be clear about your availability.

You don’t need Federal Work-Study to apply: the Student Assistant Program is another option, and U.S. citizens, permanent resident aliens, and students on F-1 visas are eligible. Work-Study is need-based, and priority for Student Assistant positions goes to students awarded Work-Study. [9][11]

1. Register on Handshake and search for open positions using the keyword “RCNJ.” Follow the instructions in each posting and contact the listed supervisor. [11]
2. The supervisor discusses the job and schedule with you; weekly hours should never conflict with classes. [12]

answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Start by deciding how many hours you can work around classes, then look for flexible part-time, seasonal, or remote roles. Prepare a simple résumé highlighting coursework, projects, volunteering, and transferable skills, and apply through job boards, nearby businesses, or your school’s career resources. Tailor each application, follow up politely, and be clear about your availability.

question: whats the policy if i miss class for a religious holiday, do i have to tell my profs ahead of time

body.answer:
Yes. If you plan to miss one or more class sessions for religious observance, you must notify your course instructor as soon as possible, and no later than before the holiday or the term’s 50% refund date, whichever comes first. This applies whether or not New Jersey recognizes the holiday. Your instructor will help you make up missed work and will not penalize you for the absence. [1]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [31]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#religious-holiday-observance1) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Where do I go if I have been issued an Interim Suspension?
When you are Interim Suspended, you must vacate the campus. In cases when you are incapacitated (unable to act on your own), your emergency contact person is notified by the On Call Administrator.
What if I am present on campus and violate the terms of the Interim Suspension?
You will be considered trespassing and will be subjected to arrest by the Mahwah Police Department. The violation will be referred to the Office of Student Conduct. You will likely face on campus disciplinary charges and may also face charges through the Mahwah Municipal Court.
What if I need to obtain clothing, books, medication, and other essential personal items from my residence room while I am serving an Interim Suspension?
You need to contact Public Safety via phone at (201) 684-7432 to make arrangements to come to campus to gather any belongings from your residence. Do not come to campus without making prior arrangements.
Am I able to attend classes when I am Interim Suspended?
No, when you are serving an Interim Suspension, you are not permitted to physically attend classes. You are banned from entering the campus.
Can I complete my coursework remotely?
You may reach out to your faculty and ask if you may complete coursework electronically or by others means that do not require you to be present on the campus. The decision to accept coursework is under the purview of the individual faculty member who oversees the course material. question: I commute about 40 min. How do I sign up for text alerts so I know if campus closes for snow before I leave home?

body.answer:
RCNJ Alerts delivers college closing notices to students’ registered phones via voice or text message and email. Students are automatically enrolled, but verify your information in the system. [11][31]

To check or update your number:
1. Go to web.ramapo.edu and log in with your Ramapo username and password.
2. Click “RCNJ Experience / Web Self Service,” then “Open General Dashboard” in “General Self-Service,” then “Personal Information.”
3. Scroll to “Phone Number,” click “Add New,” select “RCNJ Alert-” (text and/or voice), enter your phone number, and click “Add.”
4. Scroll to “Emergency Contact,” click “Add New,” and enter information for at least one emergency contact.
5. Visit the [RCNJ Alerts Login](https://rcnjpublicsafety.app.regroup.com/login), log in with your Ramapo College username and password, and verify your contact profile. [29]

You can also check college closing information on the [Ramapo website](https://www.ramapo.edu/) or call 201-236-2902. [6][8]

- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [33]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [33]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/poerd/employee-handbook/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/poerd/unit-head-handbook/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/student-handbook/official-communications-2/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/campus-safety/rcnj-alerts/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/campus-safety/rcnj-alerts/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

RCNJ Alerts delivers college closing notices to students’ registered phones via voice or text message and email. Students are automatically enrolled, but verify your information in the system. [11][31]

To check or update your number:
1. Go to web.ramapo.edu and log in with your Ramapo username and password.
2. Click “RCNJ Experience / Web Self Service,” then “Open General Dashboard” in “General Self-Service,” then “Personal Information.”
3. Scroll to “Phone Number,” click “Add New,” select “RCNJ Alert-” (text and/or voice), enter your phone number, and click “Add.”
4. Scroll to “Emergency Contact,” click “Add New,” and enter information for at least one emergency contact.
5. Visit the [RCNJ Alerts Login](https://rcnjpublicsafety.app.regroup.com/login), log in with your Ramapo College username and password, and verify your contact profile. [29]

You can also check college closing information on the [Ramapo website](https://www.ramapo.edu/) or call 201-236-2902. [6][8]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [33]

question: my grandma passed and im gonna miss like a week of classes. is there an office that lets all my professors know or do i have to email each one myself

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

The Dean of Students Office does not normally notify professors; it is your responsibility to contact each professor and let them know you will miss class. [7]

**Dean of Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7457. Email: deanofstudents@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [30]

These offices can help:
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [31]
- **Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [31]

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: who do i contact abt ramapo scholarships for next yr? like is there one application for all of them and when is it due

body.answer:
If you mean Fall 2027 as an incoming first-year student, contact Admissions. All first-year applicants are automatically considered for merit-based scholarships; no separate application is necessary. Submit your application by December 15, 2026, and ensure all required credentials are received by January 3, 2027. [1]

If you mean scholarships to apply for as a continuing student, the General Application is the first step to qualify: [https://ramapo.academicworks.com/](https://ramapo.academicworks.com/). The listed deadline for 2026/27 was September 23, 2026, so it has passed. A new application is needed each academic year. [2][3] Contact Scholarships for help with those opportunities.

**Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [31]

question: does ramapo do free tax help for students? first yr doing my own taxes w my job n idk what im doing

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Gather your income forms (such as W‑2s or 1099s), records of deductions or credits, and last year’s return. Use reputable tax-preparation software or the official tax agency’s free filing option, enter your details carefully, and check whether you need to file federal, state, or local returns. Review the return and save copies of everything; if you have self-employment income, unusual investments, or a complicated situation, consider a qualified tax professional. Deadlines and rules vary by country and location, so verify the current requirements where you live.

I don’t have verified information about free tax-preparation help for students. Ramapo says it can’t provide individual tax advice; for tax-credit questions, contact a tax preparer or advisor. [1] Payroll also can’t provide individual tax guidance and recommends contacting a personal tax advisor. [8]

**Payroll**: Phone: (201) 684-7783. Email: payroll@ramapo.edu. Office: D-119. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/taxinfo/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/payroll/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

How do I do my own taxes?

answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Gather your income forms (such as W‑2s or 1099s), records of deductions or credits, and last year’s return. Use reputable tax-preparation software or the official tax agency’s free filing option, enter your details carefully, and check whether you need to file federal, state, or local returns. Review the return and save copies of everything; if you have self-employment income, unusual investments, or a complicated situation, consider a qualified tax professional. Deadlines and rules vary by country and location, so verify the current requirements where you live.

I don’t have verified information about free tax-preparation help for students. Ramapo says it can’t provide individual tax advice; for tax-credit questions, contact a tax preparer or advisor. [1] Payroll also can’t provide individual tax guidance and recommends contacting a personal tax advisor. [8]

question: is there a commuter lounge somewhere w a microwave? and r there lockers i can use so i dont have to carry everything to my car

body.answer:
Commuter Affairs is in SC-202. [1]

Commuter Affairs's page "Is there anywhere to relax between classes?" says: "J. Lee’s is the unofficial Commuter Lounge where students can kick back and relax before or after classes. J. Lee’s features video games, a pool table, a ping pong table, and FREE POPCORN! It is located in the student center on the second floor between the Student Government office and the Black Student Union office." [2]

Commuter Affairs's page "Commuter Resources" says: "J.Lee’s: If you’re looking for a fun spot to hangout in between classes, connect with friends, or enjoy some free popcorn, head to J.Lee’s during your time at Ramapo. Located on the second floor of the student center next to the Black Student Union & Student Government Association (SGA) office, RCNJ Commuters are welcomed to enjoy a variety of activities including ping pong, pool, & video games like the PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, & retro games (PS3, Nintendo Wii, & More!) for a fun day. Commuter Connections: Want to stay in the know about events happening this semester?" (more on its page) [3]

Center for Student Involvement is in SC-202. [4]

Center for Student Involvement's page "Locker Rentals" says: "Students may come to the Student Center Office to rent small or medium lockers for use during the academic semesters. The lockers are located in the second-floor stairwell area, between B and C buildings. The rental fee is $10.00 for the semester and $20.00 for the academic year. A key is issued with payment and must be returned at the end of the semester." [5]

I don't have verified information about that part.

question: can u vape on campus or is it totally banned? is there anywhere u r allowed

body.answer:
Vaping is not totally banned outdoors. Vapes and e-cigarettes are prohibited in any campus building, and smoking is prohibited indoors or within 25 feet of any building. You may vape outside, in accordance with the campus smoking policy. [3]

Contact Housing & Residence Life if you need clarification about where outside vaping is allowed.

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [28]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

The purpose of the Alcohol, Cannabis, Other Drug, and Good Samaritan Policy (herein after “the policy”) is to define and communicate, to all members of the College, acceptable and unacceptable behavior with regards to alcohol, cannabis andother drugs and the sanctions for policy violations. The policy provides specific scenarios and examples for students of what they may do and may not do with regards to alcohol on campus. Students who are under the age of 21 may not be in possession of or in the presence of alcohol, cannabis, or other drugs at any time. Persons who are present, within college housing, where alcohol, cannabis, or other drugs are being consumed by those over or under the age of 21 will be presumed to have been consuming, in possession of, or in the presence of alcohol, cannabis, or other drugs if Public Safety Officers, On-Call Administrators or Resident Assistants are called to the scene. Hosting large gatherings or parties, where alcohol, cannabis, or other drugs are present, is considered a violation of the policy and will lead to disciplinary action, including suspension of residence privileges. The policy outlines recommended sanctions for violations of the policy.
Items commonly associated with alcohol consumption may be prohibited if they are used in a manner that violates college policies. This includes but is not limited to drinking game equipment (e.g., beer pong tables, cups arranged for drinking games) and devices designed to facilitate rapid alcohol consumption (e.g., funnels, bongs, shot glasses, or similar items when used with alcohol). While some items may be permitted if unused, their presence in a setting that suggests or promotes excessive alcohol consumption may be subject to review by college staff. Additionally, any form of excessive drinking, including but not limited to drinking games, is strictly prohibited campus-wide.

question: did my orgo grade get posted yet and whats my gpa now

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I can’t verify whether your orgo grade has posted or calculate your current GPA from the information here. To check your grade, log in through the Experience Webapp ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), select “FINAL GRADES” under the Student Records Menu, then select “Term” to view grades. [18]

To see posted grades on your transcript: visit web.ramapo.edu ([http://web.ramapo.edu/](http://web.ramapo.edu/)), click the red “Web Self Service/Web Registration” tile, then “Enter Secure Area” and sign in with your Ramapo email username and password. Click “Student Services and Financial Aid,” then “Student Profile,” then “Academic Transcript.” Choose “all levels” for transcript levels and “internal” for transcript type, and view the transcript with grades. [1]

GPA is total quality points divided by total GPA hours attempted. [2]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [33]

question: r they gonna raise tuition again next year? trying to figure out if i can afford to stay

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

The College has not confirmed whether tuition will rise next year. Tuition and fee rates are subject to Board of Trustees approval each year, typically in late June. The 2026–27 rates have been approved; see the [Cost Information page](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/costinfo/). [9][11]

To estimate what you’d pay, use your direct cost: tuition and fees, plus room and board if you live on campus. Your College Financing Plan shows estimated costs and grants and scholarships. [3][7]

Ramapo lists payment plans and financial aid options to help students stay enrolled. See [Affordability](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/affordability/). [10]

For help assessing your bill and options, contact Student Accounts or Financial Aid.

- **Board of Trustees**: Email: trustee@ramapo.edu. [31]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [31]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/understanding-your-financial-aid-award/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/understanding-your-financial-aid-award/spring-admits/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/affordability/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/costinfo/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my sleep schedule is so cooked rn, im going to bed at like 4am every night n i have 9am classes. how do i fix it

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're going through that. It's okay to not be okay, and you don't have to handle it alone.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Shift your bedtime and wake-up time gradually—about 15–30 minutes earlier or later every few days—and keep the wake-up time steady, even on weekends. Get bright outdoor light soon after waking, keep evenings dim, and avoid caffeine late in the day and long or late naps. Give yourself a relaxing wind-down routine and enough time for sleep; if sleep problems persist or seriously affect daily life, talk with a doctor.

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [1]

question: how do i budget when i only make like $200 a week from my job, i always run out of money b4 payday n end up eating ramen for 3 days

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Try a simple payday plan: list your essential bills and their due dates, then set aside money for those first. Divide what’s left by the days until your next paycheck and use that as a daily spending limit; track each purchase in your phone or on paper. If bills are irregular, save a small amount from each check toward them, and look for one expense you can pause or reduce. If essentials still cost more than your income, budgeting alone may not fix it—check whether you qualify for local food, housing, or utility assistance.

These offices can help:
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [1]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do u convert celsius to fahrenheit in ur head, my friend from abroad keeps saying its 5 degrees out and i have no idea what that means

body.answer: **General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): For a quick estimate, double the Celsius number and add 30: 5°C is about 40°F. The exact conversion is °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32, so 5°C is 41°F—chilly, but above freezing.

calls.given: How do you convert Celsius to Fahrenheit in your head? My friend from abroad keeps saying it's 5 degrees out, and I have no idea what that means.

answer: **General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): For a quick estimate, double the Celsius number and add 30: 5°C is about 40°F. The exact conversion is °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32, so 5°C is 41°F—chilly, but above freezing.

question: i get panic attacks before exams sometimes, how do i calm down when it starts?? also is there anyone at ramapo i can talk to late at nite if its really bad n counseling is closed

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're going through that. It's okay to not be okay, and you don't have to handle it alone.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Try breathing out slowly, making each exhale a little longer than your inhale, and remind yourself: “This feels frightening, but it will pass.” Press your feet into the floor and name five things you see, four things you feel, and three things you hear. Move somewhere quieter or sit down if you can; avoid trying to force the sensations away. If this is new, feels different from usual, or you may be in immediate danger, seek urgent medical help; a doctor can help if these episodes keep happening.

When it starts, take a few deep breaths to calm yourself. [5]

If you need someone late at night, Counseling Services offers emergency counseling 24/7/365. Call the main line at 201-684-7522 and follow the prompt (“Press 2”) for immediate assistance. You can also call or text 988, call 911, or go to your local emergency room. [1][3]

For a non-emergency conversation, Counseling Services has free, confidential drop-in consultations Monday-Friday, 1-3 pm in Academic Building D, room 216; last meeting begins at 2:40 pm. No appointment is necessary; students are seen first-come, first-served. Call 201-684-7522 during drop-in hours for in-person or telehealth. [4]

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [30]

On campus, these published numbers can also help:
**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**: \(201\) 684-6666; \(201\) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); \(201\) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD). [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

College is NOT vocational training. You definitely should be focusing on skill development, but what skills are the most important? How do you develop them? Recent studies have shown that people entering the workforce today can expect to have as many as five separate careers! How can you prepare for all of them? The following questions ask you about your transferable skills. Below are examples of how you can improve on these skills and how they are directly linked to your future success. Develop these and you will be prepared for whatever situation your future brings.
How well do you write?
This does not end with passing English. How well do you express yourself? Can you summarize your accomplishments and describe yourself in an intelligent and insightful way? You will have plenty of opportunity while at Ramapo to polish your writing skills. Improve now when you are in this nurturing environment. If your resume or cover letter is grammatically incorrect, or your field reports are scattered ramblings, you’ll not be told to get tutoring, you’ll just be unemployed. Write with care. The more you practice, the better you will write.
How well do you speak?
This excludes buzzwords and the latest cliche. “I’m a people person” doesn’t really separate you from the maddening crowd. Be careful not to pick up habits like ending every statement as if it where a question? It can erode your credibility. If you can’t talk with some fluency about subjects in which you specialize, then why would a company want to hire you? Everyone gets nervous speaking in public. Truthfully, the more you do it, the easier it becomes. Take a speech class, or try out for a play. Use the required presentations you’ll have in your classes as opportunities to improve your public speaking skills.
How well do you listen?
Do you listen selectively? In a job interview, do you focus on the vacation time and drift off when your interviewer describes what projects will be your responsibility? Make sure you focus. If you should, take notes. Paying attention to someone is the greatest form of flattery, and you might be surprised on how much detailed information you remember. At school, you practice this every time you listen to a lecture and take good notes. Focus.
Can you make a decision?
You practice doing this by choosing your major. You make many decisions every day. Should you study for your midterm or write your research paper? Should you take Anthropology or Psychology? Don’t be passive. Participate in making the decisions that affect your life. You would be surprised how many people are actually more comfortable having someone else tell them what is right for them. You live your life, no one else. You make the choices. Take advice from people you respect, but make your own decision.
Can you think on your feet?
You can develop this skill best pressure situations.
