I'm sorry you're going through that. It's okay to not be okay, and you don't have to handle it alone.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Try breathing out slowly, making each exhale a little longer than your inhale, and remind yourself: “This feels frightening, but it will pass.” Press your feet into the floor and name five things you see, four things you feel, and three things you hear. Move somewhere quieter or sit down if you can; avoid trying to force the sensations away. If this is new, feels different from usual, or you may be in immediate danger, seek urgent medical help; a doctor can help if these episodes keep happening.

When it starts, take a few deep breaths to calm yourself. [5]

If you need someone late at night, Counseling Services offers emergency counseling 24/7/365. Call the main line at 201-684-7522 and follow the prompt (“Press 2”) for immediate assistance. You can also call or text 988, call 911, or go to your local emergency room. [1][3]

question: lowkey really homesick, first semester and my fam is 3 hrs away. is this normal or is smth wrong w me

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Feeling homesick doesn’t mean something is wrong with you. Ramapo’s Counseling Center says students can come in to discuss loneliness and other concerns; you don’t need to have a serious psychological problem [6]. Counseling Services helps with normal developmental issues and stressors, and with adjustment to and engagement within the college community [4]. For individual counseling, call 201-684-7522 or stop by room D-216 [7].

You could also look for ways to connect: Ramapo has more than 160 student clubs and organizations [11], and first-year students are placed in residence halls intended to help them meet students with similar interests and form relationships [28].

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [33]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/training-programs/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/faq/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/faq/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/admitted-students/fun/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/student-info/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Student Freedom
Students are expected to be responsible for their choices and, thus, need to have good problem solving, self-advocacy, decision making, and communication skills. Support systems are available in college (e.g., academic advising, supplemental instruction, academic learning centers, resident assistant, disability services staff), but the student must seek those out, ask for help, and follow-through.
Life Skills
Students who begin college after high school may not only be adjusting to a new learning environment but very possibly, even a new city and friends. It may be the first time they are living on their own. They may need to learn to budget their money, cook, maintain an apartment, and learn how to live with a roommate.
Peer Network
If peers do not attend the same college, students may be without a support system of friends. During high school students often depend on their family and peers for support in problem-solving, decision making and day-to-day activities, thus they may need a new support network. College activities, organizations, and support groups can help to build new networks.

question: how do noise cancelling headphones actually work, like how does it just delete sound

body.answer: **General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Noise-cancelling headphones don’t delete sound; they reduce how much of it reaches your ears. Tiny microphones pick up outside noise, and the headphones create a sound wave that’s opposite in timing and shape, so the waves partly cancel each other out. This works best for steady low sounds, like an engine hum; sudden or high-pitched sounds are harder to cancel.

question: my roommates gf basically lives in our room now, shes there like every night. how do i bring it up w/o it being super awkward

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Keep it simple and low-pressure: choose a calm moment, say what’s on your mind plainly, and give them room to respond. You could start with, “Hey, can I bring something up? It’s a little awkward, but I’d rather talk about it.”

Try bringing it up privately and calmly: “Hey, can we talk about overnight guests? I’ve noticed your girlfriend is here most nights, and I’m not comfortable with how often it’s happening. Can we agree on expectations that work for both of us?” Ramapo recommends open conversations about guest expectations. Roommates have the right to sleep without unnecessary disturbances, privacy, and to host guests as long as guest policies are followed and others’ rights are respected. [1][2]

Guests may stay no more than three nights within a seven-day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. [2] If you can’t agree, contact your Resident Assistant to help facilitate a roommate contract; RAs can mediate resident conflicts. [2][10]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [31]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/residences/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Keep it simple and low-pressure: choose a calm moment, say what’s on your mind plainly, and give them room to respond. You could start with, “Hey, can I bring something up? It’s a little awkward, but I’d rather talk about it.”

Try bringing it up privately and calmly: “Hey, can we talk about overnight guests? I’ve noticed your girlfriend is here most nights, and I’m not comfortable with how often it’s happening. Can we agree on expectations that work for both of us?” Ramapo recommends open conversations about guest expectations. Roommates have the right to sleep without unnecessary disturbances, privacy, and to host guests as long as guest policies are followed and others’ rights are respected. [1][2]

Guests may stay no more than three nights within a seven-day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. [2] If you can’t agree, contact your Resident Assistant to help facilitate a roommate contract; RAs can mediate resident conflicts. [2][10]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [31]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/residences/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: any tips for staying awake driving home for thanksgiving its like a 4 hr drive. n do i have to do anything w my dorm room b4 i leave for break like unplug stuff

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): The safest tip is not to drive drowsy: if you’re sleepy, pull over somewhere safe and rest, or switch drivers. Get a full night’s sleep before leaving, take breaks about every couple of hours, and avoid alcohol or sedating medicines. Caffeine may help briefly but won’t replace sleep; if you’re struggling to keep your eyes open, stop driving.

I don’t have verified tips for staying awake on a four-hour drive. Ramapo’s guidance says don’t drive distracted or after consuming alcohol or other drugs, and don’t use your cell phone while driving. [26]

Before leaving for break: remove trash and recyclables (fines start at $25 per bundle); unplug your personal items, but do not unplug College items (refrigerator and desk lights). Leave the College refrigerator on at level 5 and remove all perishables. Set the thermostat to auto, low, at 70°F. Take valuables and needed supplies, close blinds, lock windows, turn off lights, and close your room door. Residents cannot re-enter their Fall 2026 housing during Winter Break, so pack accordingly, including medicine, chargers, and documents. Not following checkout requirements may result in a $75 fine. Review the [check-out checklist](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/check-out-checklist/). [1][2]

For questions about your room checkout, contact Housing & Residence Life.

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [35]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/check-out-checklist/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/ehs/pedestrian-safety/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do u cite a website in apa if theres no author? n does the ramapo library have like a citation guide or smth

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): In APA 7, move the webpage title into the author position, followed by the date and site name: *Title of webpage*. (Year, Month Day). Site Name. URL. If the site name is the same as the title, leave it out; if there’s no date, use “(n.d.).” In-text, cite a shortened title in quotation marks, like (“Shortened Title,” 2023).

I don’t have verified information here on how to format an APA website citation when there’s no author. The Library’s citation page links to the Purdue OWL APA Style Guide: [https://owl.english.purdue.edu/owl/resource/560/01/](https://owl.english.purdue.edu/owl/resource/560/01/) [3]. The entry begins with the title of the article (in this case, a biography of Woody Guthrie) and is followed by the title of the page. Next, the entry lists the institution associated with the site. Again, ideally, one would follow this with the date the page was “published.” However, this information is frequently not given on web pages. Then follows the date the writer accessed the information. Finally the entry lists the URL.
When listing the URL, the writer should be careful not to break the address up; try to include the entire address in one line of text. If I must break the address and continue it on the next line, one should break at a slash (“/”) and not insert a hyphen. To insure accuracy in transcription, it might be a good idea to cut the address from the web and paste it directly into the paper.
Citing an online text also available in a traditional edition
Increasingly, literary texts are becoming available in on-line forms. Using these sources can be quite convenient, even if they are not quite as much fun when curling up in front of a warm fire. However, it is worth keeping in mind that traditional books are going to be more reliable, especially if they are published by a reputable publishing company and edited by a professional. Still, when citing online texts, there are documentation protocols one needs to follow:
James, Henry. Hawthorne . 1879. 1 Aug. 2000. <http://eldred.ne.mediaone.net/hjj/nhhj1.html>
In this case, the web page gives no information regarding the source of the text. Had they done so, the entry would include that information after the title. The site does, however, list the date of original publication, so that information is included.

Bacon, Katie. “An African Voice.” Interview with Chinua Achebe Atlantic Unbound . 2 Aug. 2000. 4 Aug. 2000.
< http://www.theAtlantic.com/ unbound/interviews/ba2000-08-02.htm. (http://www.theatlantic.com/%20%20unbound/interviews/ba2000-08-02.htm.)>
As with a print magazine article, the entry cites author, title, magazine title, and publication information. Also included is the URL and two dates. The first is the date the article initially appeared. The second is the date the writer accessed the information.
Citing an article from an on-line scholarly journal
Helming, Steven. “Failure and the Sublime: Fredric Jameson’s Writing in the 80’s.” Postmodern Culture 10.3 (2000) 4 Aug. 2000
< http://www.iath.virginia.edu/pmc/ current.issue/10.3helming.html (http://www.iath.virginia.edu/pmc/%20current.issue/10.3helming.html)>
The citation documents author, title, journal title, volume and number, date of publication, and date of access. The citation concludes with the URL.

How do you cite a website in APA if there's no author?

answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): In APA 7, move the webpage title into the author position, followed by the date and site name: *Title of webpage*. (Year, Month Day). Site Name. URL. If the site name is the same as the title, leave it out; if there’s no date, use “(n.d.).” In-text, cite a shortened title in quotation marks, like (“Shortened Title,” 2023).

I don’t have verified information here on how to format an APA website citation when there’s no author. The Library’s citation page links to the Purdue OWL APA Style Guide: [https://owl.english.purdue.edu/owl/resource/560/01/](https://owl.english.purdue.edu/owl/resource/560/01/) [3]. The library site also has a Citation link: [https://www.ramapo.edu/library/citation-help/](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/citation-help/) [2].
